column1: # SET-LEVEL COLLISIONS — names that are each legal and still cannot coexist.
# Explained for app developers in docs/WORLD-CONSTRAINTS.md. That page describes
# this file; this file defines the rules. If they disagree, the page is the bug.
# WHY A SEPARATE FILE FROM VECTORS.tsv. Those rows judge ONE name. These judge a
# SET, and the difference is the whole point: every name below is individually
# fine. The bug only exists in the relationship between two of them, which is
# invisible to any per-name check no matter how strict.
# The host does not report these. One file becomes the other, or shadows it in a
# listing — so this is found by a person wondering where their save went.
# FORMAT: <space-separated names> <TAB> <verdict>
# verdict is `ok`, or how the first colliding pair collides:
#   case-fold   — identical once case is folded; one file on FAT/Windows/macOS
#   short-name  — identical once truncated to a FAT 8.3 short name
# CASE ORDER MATTERS: when a pair collides both ways, `case-fold` is reported,
# because "these differ only in case" is the more useful thing to be told.
# --- distinct names, which must keep working ------------------------------
hello tictactoe notes
only
abcdefg1 abcdefg2
save.json board.json
a b c d e f g
# --- 8.3 truncation: LIVE, not hypothetical -------------------------------
# The badge renders a catalog name as its first EIGHT characters, so these
# appear on the USB volume as one file and the second is unreachable.
board-state-1 board-state-2
abcdefgh1 abcdefgh2
hello-world-alpha hello-world-beta
# --- sanitisation CREATING a collision ------------------------------------
# Two different legal names becoming one short name because the bytes that
# distinguished them were replaced. This is why a validator must call the
# renderer's own truncation rather than compare the original strings.
a.b a_b
# Cannot arise under the portable profile, which forbids uppercase. This is the
# trade an app makes by declaring the narrower `posix` world.
save.json Save.json
readme README
# --- the pair is what gets named, not the set -----------------------------
alpha beta board-state-1 gamma board-state-2
